correctness.rationale: Exact singular-value diagonalization of the n-by-m bidiagonal hopping T yields simple nonzero energies and one fully normalized chiral zero mode. The dissipative semigroup on the complement of loss-free Hermitian eigenvectors has strictly negative spectral imaginary parts and exponentially vanishing norm, so sitewise capture equals the bright projector diagonal. Simultaneous minority-site nodal conditions reduce by Bézout to g-1 positive-energy mode pairs. The sum over sine squares equals g/n unless g divides the source index. The majority-site nodal condition gives a finite positive ratio set; endpoints have none. The executable verifier checks 1135 rank cases, 2260 sitewise captures, 32 direct lossy spectra, an exact polynomial gcd and 4 finite-time convergence examples. Universal statements come from proof, not enumeration.

value.rationale: The nontrivial parameter-independent dark-count law for arbitrary detector subsets and explicit sitewise survival solve a natural detector-placement question in bipartite quantum transport. Its gcd boundary reveals monitor choices that cannot remove additional dark pairs, while majority-sublattice resonances show precise sensitivity to hopping ratios. The self-contained finite-chain classification is directly usable for placing lossy sensors; not a table recomputation or trivial edge-mode normalization.
